title.zh: 卷一百十七 列傳第六十七: 嚴武 郭英乂 崔寧 嚴震 嚴礪
title.en: Volume 117 Biographies 67: Yan Wu, Guo Yingyi, Cui Ning, Yan Zhen, Yan Li
title.raw: 卷一百十七 列傳第六十七: 嚴武 郭英乂 崔寧 嚴震 嚴礪 Volume 117 Biographies 67: Yan Wu, Guo Yingyi, Cui Ning, Yan Zhen, Yan Li

sentences.zh: 嚴武，中書侍郎挺之子也。

translations.literal: Yan Wu was the son of Ting, Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wu was the son of Ting, who had served as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 神氣雋爽，敏於聞見。

translations.literal: His spirit and bearing were sharp and lofty, and he was quick in what he heard and observed.
translations.idiomatic: He had a keen, commanding presence and was unusually quick to grasp what he heard and saw.

sentences.zh: 幼有成人之風，讀書不究精義，涉獵而已。

translations.literal: In youth he had the manner of a grown man; in reading he did not pursue the deepest meanings but merely ranged broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he carried himself like an adult; he read widely but never troubled to master texts in depth.

sentences.zh: 弱冠以門廕策名，隴右節度使哥舒翰奏充判官，遷侍御史。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the capping age he entered the rolls through hereditary privilege; the Longyou Military Commissioner Geshu Han memorialized to appoint him as aide, and he was promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At his coming of age he qualified through family privilege; Geshu Han, military commissioner of Longyou, had him appointed as aide on memorial and then promoted him to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 至德初，肅宗興師靖難，大收才傑，武杖節赴行在。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhide era, when Emperor Suzong raised armies to quell the rebellion and gathered outstanding men on a large scale, Wu took the staff of office and went to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhide reign, as Emperor Suzong mobilized to put down the rebellion and recruited talent far and wide, Wu took up his commission and hurried to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 宰相房琯以武名臣之子，素重之，及是，首薦才略可稱，累遷給事中。

translations.literal: The Chief Minister Fang Guan, because Wu was the son of a famous minister, had long valued him; on this occasion he was the first to recommend that his talent and strategy were commendable, and Wu was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Fang Guan had always held Wu in esteem as the son of a distinguished official; now he was first to recommend him for his ability and was instrumental in promoting him repeatedly until he reached Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 既收長安，以武為京兆少尹、兼御史中丞，時年三十二。

translations.literal: After Chang'an was recovered, Wu was made Vice Governor of Jingzhao and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief; he was then thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chang'an had been retaken, he was appointed Vice Governor of the capital district and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief at the age of thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 以史思明阻兵不之官，優遊京師，頗自矜大。

translations.literal: Because Shi Siming obstructed the roads with his troops, he did not take up the post but idled in the capital, quite self-important.
translations.idiomatic: With Shi Siming's armies blocking the routes, he never took up his post and instead lingered in the capital, growing rather full of himself.

sentences.zh: 出為綿州刺史，遷劍南東川節度使；

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Mianzhou and was transferred to Military Commissioner of Jiannan East Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as prefect of Mianzhou and later promoted to military commissioner of eastern Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 入為太子賓客、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Guest of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as a guest of the heir apparent and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 上皇誥以劍兩川合為一道，拜武成都尹、兼御史大夫，充劍南節度使；

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor issued an edict that the two circuits of Jiannan be united into one; Wu was appointed Governor of Chengdu, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and made Military Commissioner of Jiannan;
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor ordered the two Jiannan circuits merged into one command; Wu was named governor of Chengdu, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and military commissioner of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 入為太子賓客，遷京兆尹、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Guest of the Heir Apparent and was transferred to Governor of Jingzhao and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as guest of the heir apparent, then was moved to governor of the capital district with the concurrent title of Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 二聖山陵，以武為橋道使。

translations.literal: For the mausoleums of the Two Sages, Wu was made Commissioner of Bridges and Roads.
translations.idiomatic: When the tombs of the two deceased emperors were under construction, he was appointed commissioner for bridges and roads.

sentences.zh: 無何，罷兼御史大夫，改吏部侍郎，尋遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was relieved of the concurrent post of Censor-in-Chief, made Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and soon transferred to Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he relinquished the concurrent censorate, became vice minister of personnel, and soon after was promoted to vice minister of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與宰臣元載深相結托，冀其引在同列。

translations.literal: He formed a deep bond with the Chief Minister Yuan Zai, hoping that Zai would bring him into the same rank.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated a close alliance with Chief Minister Yuan Zai in the hope that Zai would elevate him to the highest council.

sentences.zh: 事未行，求為方面，復拜成都尹，充劍南節度等使。

translations.literal: The matter had not been carried out when he requested a regional post; he was again appointed Governor of Chengdu and made Military Commissioner of Jiannan and related offices.
translations.idiomatic: Before that plan could succeed he asked for a frontier command and was again named governor of Chengdu and military commissioner of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年，破吐蕃七萬余眾，拔當狗城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangde he defeated more than seventy thousand Tibetans and captured Danggou Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In 764 he routed over seventy thousand Tibetan troops and took Danggou Fort.

sentences.zh: 十月，取鹽川城，加檢校吏部尚書，封鄭國公。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he took Yanchuan Fort, was given the additional title of Acting Minister of Personnel, and enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: That October he seized Yanchuan Fort, received the additional appointment as acting minister of personnel, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 前後在蜀累年，肆誌逞欲，恣行猛政。

translations.literal: Over many years before and after in Shu he indulged his will and desires and arbitrarily carried out harsh government.
translations.idiomatic: During his long years in Shu he gave free rein to his appetites and ruled with arbitrary severity.

sentences.zh: 梓州刺史章彜初為武判官，及是小不副意，赴成都杖殺之，由是威震一方。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, Prefect of Zizhou, had first been Wu's aide; when he fell slightly short of Wu's wishes, Wu had him brought to Chengdu and beaten to death with the staff, and from this his awe filled the region.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi of Zizhou had once served as his aide; when Yi displeased him even slightly, Wu summoned him to Chengdu and had him clubbed to death, and thereafter his terror held the whole region.

sentences.zh: 蜀土頗饒珍產，武窮極奢靡，賞賜無度，或由一言賞至百萬。

translations.literal: The land of Shu was quite rich in rare products; Wu pursued luxury to the extreme, his rewards without limit, and sometimes for a single remark he would grant up to a million.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was rich in rare goods, and Wu spent without limit; a single pleasing word from him could bring a reward of a million cash.

sentences.zh: 蜀方閭裏以征斂殆至匱竭，然蕃虜亦不敢犯境。

translations.literal: In the villages of Shu, levies brought them nearly to exhaustion, yet the barbarians of the frontier also did not dare to violate the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes and levies nearly beggared the countryside, yet frontier tribes likewise dared not cross his borders.

sentences.zh: 而性本狂蕩，視事多率胸臆，雖慈母言不之顧。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was fundamentally reckless; in conducting affairs he mostly followed his breast and belly, and even his loving mother's words he did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was headstrong and impulsive, governing mostly on whim; he would not even listen to his own mother.

sentences.zh: 初為劍南節度使，舊相房琯出為管內刺史，琯於武有薦導之恩，武驕倨，見琯略無朝禮，甚為時議所貶。

translations.literal: When he first became Military Commissioner of Jiannan, the former Chief Minister Fang Guan went out as a prefect within the circuit; Guan had the grace of recommending and guiding Wu, but Wu was arrogant and haughty and on seeing Guan showed hardly any court etiquette, and this was much decried in contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took command in Jiannan, his former patron Fang Guan was serving as a circuit prefect; though Guan had launched his career, Wu treated him with arrogant disrespect and scarcely a trace of formal courtesy, drawing widespread condemnation.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年四月，以疾終，時年四十。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongtai he died of illness; he was then forty.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the fourth month of 765, at the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 郭英乂

translations.literal: Guo Yingyi
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yingyi

sentences.zh: 郭英乂，先朝隴右節度使、左羽林軍將軍知運之季子也。

translations.literal: Guo Yingyi was the youngest son of Zhiyun, former Military Commissioner of Longyou and General of the Left Forest Army.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yingyi was the youngest son of Zhiyun, who had served as military commissioner of Longyou and general of the Left Forest Army.

sentences.zh: 少以父業，習知武藝，策名河、隴間，以軍功累遷諸衛員外將軍。

translations.literal: In youth through his father's profession he learned military arts, entered the rolls between the Yellow River and Longyou, and through military merit was repeatedly promoted to Outside General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his father's trade, mastered the military arts, made his name on the northwest frontier, and rose through battlefield merit to outside general in the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 至德初，肅宗興師朔野，英乂以將門子特見任用，遷隴右節度使、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide, when Emperor Suzong raised armies in the northern wilds, Yingyi as the son of a general family was especially employed and was transferred to Military Commissioner of Longyou and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhide reign, when Suzong campaigned in the north, Yingyi was singled out for appointment as a general's son and made military commissioner of Longyou with the concurrent vice censorate.

sentences.zh: 既收二京，征還闕下，掌禁兵。

translations.literal: After the Two Capitals were recovered, he was summoned back to the court and placed in charge of the forbidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were retaken he was recalled to court to command the palace armies.

sentences.zh: 遷羽林軍大將軍，加特進。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand General of the Forest Army and given the extraordinary promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand general of the Forest Army and granted the extraordinary rank of tejin.

sentences.zh: 以家艱去職。

translations.literal: He left office on account of family mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方討史思明，選任將帥，乃起英乂為陜州刺史，充陜西節度、潼關防禦等使，尋加御史大夫，兼神策軍節度。

translations.literal: The court was then campaigning against Shi Siming and selecting commanders; Yingyi was recalled as Prefect of Shaanzhou, made Military Commissioner of Shaanxi, Defender of Tong Pass, and related offices, and soon given Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Military Commissioner of the Divine Strategy Army.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was fighting Shi Siming it recalled him as prefect of Shaanzhou, gave him command of Shaanxi and Tong Pass, and soon added the censorate and command of the Divine Strategy Army.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，加檢校戶部尚書、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong took the throne, he was given the additional title of Acting Minister of Revenue and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On Daizong's accession he received the additional posts of acting minister of revenue and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 元帥雍王自陜統諸軍討賊洛陽，留英乂在陜為後殿。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yong as commander-in-chief led the armies from Shaan to attack the rebels at Luoyang, leaving Yingyi at Shaan as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yong marched from Shaan to attack the rebels at Luoyang, Yingyi was left behind to guard the rear.

sentences.zh: 東都平，以英乂權為東都留守。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, Yingyi was made acting Eastern Capital Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Luoyang was secured he was appointed acting intendant of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 既至東都，不能禁暴，縱麾下兵與朔方、回紇之眾大掠都城，延及鄭、汝等州，比屋蕩盡。

translations.literal: Once he reached the Eastern Capital he could not restrain violence; he let his subordinate troops together with the Shuo-fang and Uyghur forces plunder the capital on a great scale, extending to Zheng, Ru, and other prefectures until house after house was swept clean.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Luoyang he failed to keep order and allowed his men, together with Shuo-fang and Uyghur troops, to sack the city and ravage Zheng, Ru, and neighboring prefectures until scarcely a household was left untouched.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，策勛加實封二百戶，征拜尚書右僕射，封定襄郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde, for recorded merit his substantive fief was increased by two hundred households; he was summoned and appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Prince of Dingxiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 763 his fief was increased by two hundred households for merit; he was recalled to court as right vice director of the department of state affairs and enfeoffed as Prince of Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 恃富而驕，於京城創起甲第，窮極奢靡。

translations.literal: Relying on wealth he was arrogant; in the capital he built a mansion of the first rank, pursuing luxury to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Flush with wealth, he grew arrogant and erected in the capital a palatial residence of staggering extravagance.

sentences.zh: 與宰臣元載交結，以久其權。

translations.literal: He formed ties with the Chief Minister Yuan Zai in order to prolong his power.
translations.idiomatic: He allied himself with Chief Minister Yuan Zai to keep his power secure.

sentences.zh: 會劍南節度使嚴武卒，載以英乂代之，兼成都尹，充劍南節度使。

translations.literal: When Military Commissioner of Jiannan Yan Wu died, Zai replaced him with Yingyi, who was also made Governor of Chengdu and Military Commissioner of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Wu died as military commissioner of Jiannan, Yuan Zai sent Yingyi to replace him as governor of Chengdu and military commissioner of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 既至成都，肆行不軌，無所忌憚。

translations.literal: Once he reached Chengdu he wantonly acted out of line and feared nothing.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Chengdu he behaved with brazen lawlessness and feared no one.

sentences.zh: 玄宗幸蜀時舊宮，置為道士觀，內有玄宗鑄金真容及乘輿侍衛圖畫。

translations.literal: The former palace from when Emperor Xuanzong visited Shu was made a Daoist abbey, containing Xuanzong's cast-gold true likeness and paintings of the imperial carriage and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The palace Xuanzong had used during his flight to Shu was converted into a Daoist temple housing his gilded portrait and paintings of the imperial procession and guard.

sentences.zh: 先是，節度使每至，皆先拜而後視事。

translations.literal: Previously, whenever a military commissioner arrived, he would first perform obeisance and only afterward conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hitherto every new commissioner had bowed before the imperial image before taking up his duties.

sentences.zh: 英乂以觀地形勝，乃入居之，其真容圖畫，悉遭毀壞。

translations.literal: Yingyi, because the abbey's terrain was superior, then moved in to dwell there; the true likeness and paintings were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the site commanding, Yingyi moved into the temple himself and had the portrait and paintings destroyed.

sentences.zh: 見者無不憤怒，以軍政苛酷，無敢發言。

translations.literal: Those who saw it were without exception furious, but because military and civil government were harsh and cruel, none dared to speak.
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed it were outraged, yet his brutal rule left no one daring to protest.

sentences.zh: 又頗恣狂蕩，聚女人騎驢擊球，制鈿驢鞍及諸服用，皆侈靡裝飾，日費數萬，以為笑樂。

translations.literal: He also rather indulged reckless dissipation, gathering women to ride donkeys and play polo; the inlaid donkey saddles and all apparel were lavishly ornamented, costing tens of thousands daily for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He further indulged in wild excesses, assembling women to play donkey polo on saddles inlaid with precious metal and decked in lavish finery, spending tens of thousands a day for sport.

sentences.zh: 未嘗問百姓間事，人頗怨之。

translations.literal: He never inquired into the affairs of the common people; the people were quite resentful.
translations.idiomatic: He never troubled himself with the people's welfare, and popular resentment ran deep.

sentences.zh: 又以西山兵馬使崔旰得眾心，屢抑之。

translations.literal: Moreover, because the Western Hills Army and Horse Commissioner Cui Gan had won the hearts of the troops, he repeatedly suppressed him.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly slighted Cui Gan, commissioner of the western hills forces, who had won the soldiers' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 旰因蜀人之怨，自西山率麾下五千余眾襲成都，英乂出軍拒之，其眾皆叛，反攻英乂。

translations.literal: Gan, relying on the resentment of the people of Shu, led more than five thousand of his followers from the Western Hills to attack Chengdu; Yingyi marched out to resist, but his troops all rebelled and turned to attack Yingyi.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on popular anger in Shu, Gan marched from the western hills with over five thousand men to strike Chengdu; Yingyi met him in the field, but his own troops mutinied and turned on him.

sentences.zh: 英乂奔於簡州，普州刺史韓澄斬英乂首以送旰，並屠其妻子焉。

translations.literal: Yingyi fled to Jian Prefecture; Han Cheng, Prefect of Puzhou, beheaded Yingyi and sent his head to Gan, and also slaughtered his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyi fled toward Jian Prefecture; Han Cheng, prefect of Puzhou, cut off his head and sent it to Gan, then massacred his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 崔寧，衛州人，本名旰。

translations.literal: Cui Ning, a native of Weizhou, original name Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning, a native of Weizhou, was originally named Gan.

sentences.zh: 雖儒家子，喜縱橫之術。

translations.literal: Although a Confucian family's son, he delighted in the arts of coalition and persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: Though raised in a scholar's household, he was drawn to the arts of political maneuver and intrigue.

sentences.zh: 衛州刺史茹璋授旰符離令，既罷，久不調，遂客遊劍南，從軍為步卒，事鮮于仲通。

translations.literal: Ru Zhang, Prefect of Weizhou, appointed Gan magistrate of Fuli; after leaving office he long received no new assignment, so he traveled as a guest in Jiannan, joined the army as a foot soldier, and served Xianyu Zhongtong.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Zhang, prefect of Weizhou, made him magistrate of Fuli; when his term ended he received no further appointment and wandered into Jiannan as a soldier under Xianyu Zhongtong.

sentences.zh: 又隨李宓討雲南，宓戰敗，旰歸成都。

translations.literal: He also followed Li Mi in campaigning against Yunnan; Mi was defeated in battle and Gan returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Li Mi's ill-fated campaign into Yunnan and returned to Chengdu after Mi's defeat.

sentences.zh: 行軍司馬崔論見旰，悅其狀貌，又以其宗姓厚遇，薦為衙將。

translations.literal: The campaigning staff officer Cui Lun saw Gan, was pleased with his appearance, and because they shared the clan name treated him generously and recommended him as a yamen general.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning staff officer Cui Lun took a liking to his bearing, favored him as a kinsman, and recommended him for a post as yamen general.

sentences.zh: 歷事崔圓、裴冕。

translations.literal: He successively served Cui Yuan and Pei Mian.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn under Cui Yuan and Pei Mian.

sentences.zh: 冕遭流謗，朝廷將遣使推按，旰部下截耳稱冤，中使奏之。

translations.literal: Mian suffered circulating slander; the court was about to send an envoy to investigate, when Gan's subordinates cut off their ears and proclaimed injustice, and the palace envoy reported this.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Mian fell victim to slander and the court prepared to send investigators, Gan's men mutilated their ears in protest of his innocence, and the palace envoy reported the affair.

sentences.zh: 旰亦赴京師，授司戈，歷司階、折沖郎將軍等官。

translations.literal: Gan also went to the capital, was appointed Lance-corporal, and passed through Lance-sergeant, Irregularly Attendant General, and other offices.
translations.idiomatic: Gan went to the capital as well, receiving appointments from lance-corporal up through irregularly attendant general.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，蜀中亂，山賊擁絕縣道，代宗憂之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying, Shu was in turmoil; mountain bandits blocked the county roads, and Emperor Daizong was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Baoying era Shu fell into disorder as mountain bandits cut the county roads, greatly worrying Emperor Daizong.

sentences.zh: 嚴武薦旰為利州刺史，既至，山賊遁散，由是知名。

translations.literal: Yan Wu recommended Gan as Prefect of Lizhou; once he arrived, the mountain bandits fled and dispersed, and from this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wu recommended him as prefect of Lizhou; on his arrival the bandits melted away, and his reputation was made.

sentences.zh: 嚴武為劍南節度，赴鎮過利州，心欲辟旰為部將，以利非屬部，旰難輒去，俾旰籌之。

translations.literal: When Yan Wu became Military Commissioner of Jiannan and passed through Lizhou on the way to his command, he wished in his heart to recruit Gan as a staff general, but because Lizhou was not under his jurisdiction Gan could not readily leave, so Wu had Gan devise a plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Wu took up the Jiannan command and passed through Lizhou, he wanted Gan on his staff, but Lizhou lay outside his circuit and Gan could not simply depart—so Wu asked him to find a way.

sentences.zh: 旰曰：「節度使張獻誠見忌，且又好利，誠能重賂之，旰可以從大夫矣。」

translations.literal: Gan said: "The Military Commissioner Zhang Xiancheng is jealous and moreover fond of profit; if you can truly bribe him heavily, Gan can follow the great man."
translations.idiomatic: Gan said, "Commissioner Zhang Xiancheng is touchy and greedy; if you reward him handsomely, I can join your staff."

sentences.zh: 武至劍南，遺獻誠奇錦珍貝，價兼百金，獻誠大悅。

translations.literal: When Wu reached Jiannan he sent Xiancheng rare brocades and precious shells worth together a hundred in gold, and Xiancheng was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Jiannan, Wu sent Xiancheng brocades and jewels worth a hundred gold pieces, to his great delight.

sentences.zh: 武乃遺獻誠書求旰，獻誠然之，令旰移疾去郡。

translations.literal: Wu then sent Xiancheng a letter requesting Gan; Xiancheng agreed and ordered Gan to leave the prefecture on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wu then wrote asking for Gan; Xiancheng consented and had Gan resign the prefecture on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 旰乃之劍南，武奏為漢州刺史。

translations.literal: Gan then went to Jiannan, and Wu memorialized to make him Prefect of Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gan then joined Wu in Jiannan, and Wu had him appointed prefect of Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，吐蕃與諸雜羌戎寇陷西山柘、靜等州，詔嚴武收復。

translations.literal: After some time, Tibetans together with various Qiang and Rong tribes invaded and captured the Western Hills prefectures Zhe, Jing, and others; an edict ordered Yan Wu to recover them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tibetans and allied Qiang and Rong tribes overran the western hills prefectures of Zhe and Jing; the court ordered Yan Wu to retake them.

sentences.zh: 武遣旰統兵西山，旰善撫士卒，皆願致死命。

translations.literal: Wu sent Gan to command troops in the Western Hills; Gan was good at comforting the soldiers, and all were willing to give their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent Gan to lead the western campaign; Gan won his men's devotion, and they were ready to die for him.

sentences.zh: 始次賊城，周圍皆石礫，攻具無所設。

translations.literal: When he first encamped before the rebel city, the surroundings were all stone and rubble, and siege equipment could not be set up.
translations.idiomatic: When he first encamped before the enemy stronghold, the ground was nothing but stone and rubble, leaving no place to deploy siege engines.

sentences.zh: 唯東南隅環丈之地，壤土可穴，諜知之以告。

translations.literal: Only on the southeast corner was a ring of land about a zhang across where the soil could be tunneled; spies learned this and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Only on the southeast corner was a patch of earth about thirty feet across suitable for tunneling, which his scouts reported.

sentences.zh: 旰晝夜穿地道攻之，再宿而拔其城。

translations.literal: Gan day and night dug a tunnel to attack; after two nights he captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: Gan dug through day and night and took the city within two days.

sentences.zh: 因拓地數百里，下城寨數四。

translations.literal: Thereby he extended territory for several hundred li and captured four or so fortified towns and stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He extended Tang control for hundreds of li and reduced four fortified posts.

sentences.zh: 番眾相語曰：「崔旰，神兵也。」

translations.literal: The barbarian masses said to one another: "Cui Gan is divine troops."
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen said among themselves, "Cui Gan commands supernatural forces."

sentences.zh: 將更前進，以糧盡還師。

translations.literal: They were about to advance further, but because provisions were exhausted they returned the army.
translations.idiomatic: They were preparing to push farther when exhausted supplies forced a withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 武大悅，裝七寶輿迎旰入成都，以誇士眾，賞賫過厚。

translations.literal: Wu was greatly pleased, fitted out a carriage of the seven treasures to welcome Gan into Chengdu to display him before the troops, and his rewards were excessively generous.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was overjoyed, sent a jeweled carriage to bring Gan into Chengdu in triumph before the troops, and lavished rewards beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年五月，嚴武卒，杜濟為西川行軍司馬，權知軍府事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yongtai, Yan Wu died. Du Ji was made campaigning staff officer of the West Circuit and acted as administrator of the military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of 765 Yan Wu died. Du Ji became campaigning staff officer of the West Circuit and provisionally administered the military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時郭英幹為都知兵馬使，郭嘉琳為都虞候，皆請英幹兄英乂為節度使。

translations.literal: At the time Guo Yinggan served as commander of military affairs and Guo Jialin as deputy commander; both petitioned for Yinggan's elder brother Yingyi as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yinggan was then commander of military affairs and Guo Jialin deputy commander; both petitioned for Yinggan's elder brother Guo Yingyi as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 旰時為西山都知兵馬使，與軍眾共請大將王崇俊為節度使。

translations.literal: Gan was then commander of military affairs in the Western Hills; together with the army he petitioned for the great general Wang Chongjun as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Gan was then Western Hills commander of military affairs; he and the troops jointly petitioned for the great general Wang Chongjun as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二奏俱至京師，會朝廷已除英乂，旰使因見英乂陳其事。

translations.literal: Both memorials reached the capital together; as it happened the court had already appointed Yingyi, and Gan's envoy took occasion to see Yingyi and explain the matter to him.
translations.idiomatic: Both petitions reached the capital together, but the court had already appointed Guo Yingyi; Gan's envoy therefore met Yingyi and explained what had happened.

sentences.zh: 英乂至成都，數日，誣殺王崇俊，又召旰還成都。

translations.literal: When Yingyi reached Chengdu, within several days he falsely accused and killed Wang Chongjun, and also summoned Gan back to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingyi reached Chengdu, within days he framed and killed Wang Chongjun and summoned Gan back to the city.

sentences.zh: 英乂減將健糧賜，人心怨怒。

translations.literal: Yingyi reduced the generous grain rations for officers and soldiers, and resentment stirred among the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyi cut the officers' and soldiers' generous grain allowances, and morale turned to anger.

sentences.zh: 旰在西山聞之，大恐，乃托備吐蕃，未赴成都。

translations.literal: Gan in the Western Hills heard of this and was greatly afraid; he made the pretext of guarding against Tibet and did not go to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Gan in the Western Hills heard this and was terrified; he pleaded readiness against Tibet and did not come to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 英乂怒，出兵聲言助旰討吐蕃，其實襲之也。

translations.literal: Yingyi was enraged and sent out troops, declaring that he was aiding Gan in attacking Tibet, but in fact intended to strike at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyi was furious and marched out, claiming he would help Gan fight Tibet but in fact meant to attack him.

sentences.zh: 旰家在漢州，英乂遷之成都，通其妾媵。

translations.literal: Gan's family was in Hanzhou; Yingyi moved them to Chengdu and violated his concubines and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Gan's family was in Hanzhou; Yingyi transferred them to Chengdu and violated his concubines and female attendants.

sentences.zh: 旰知之，轉入深山。

translations.literal: When Gan learned of this, he fled into the deep mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Gan learned of this, he withdrew into the deep mountains.

sentences.zh: 英乂自率師攻旰，值天大寒，雪深數尺，英乂士馬凍死者數百人，眾心離叛。

translations.literal: Yingyi personally led troops to attack Gan; heaven sent intense cold, snow piled several chi deep, and several hundred of Yingyi's men and horses froze to death, so hearts turned away in mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyi personally led an attack on Gan. Bitter cold set in and snow piled several feet deep; several hundred of his men and horses froze to death, and his troops began to desert.

sentences.zh: 旰遂出兵拒敵，英乂與之接戰，英乂軍大敗而還，收余兵才千人，歸成都，將卒因多逃散。

translations.literal: Gan thereupon sent out troops to resist; Yingyi engaged him in battle, Yingyi's army was utterly defeated and retreated, gathering barely a thousand remnant troops before returning to Chengdu, where officers and soldiers mostly deserted and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Gan then marched out to resist. Yingyi met him in battle and was routed; he gathered barely a thousand survivors and returned to Chengdu, where most of his officers and soldiers deserted.

sentences.zh: 初，天寶中，劍南節度使鮮于仲通嘗建一使院，院宇甚華麗。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Tianbao era, the Military Commissioner of Jiannan Xianyu Zhongtong had once built a commissionerate compound, its buildings very splendid.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign, military commissioner Xianyu Zhongtong had built a splendid headquarters compound in Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 及玄宗幸蜀，嘗居之，因為道觀，兼寫玄宗真容，置之正室。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong visited Shu he had once dwelt there; it was therefore made a Daoist abbey, and Xuanzong's true likeness was also painted and placed in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong fled to Shu he had stayed there; the building was later converted to a Daoist temple with his portrait installed in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 英乂因入觀行香，悅其竹樹，遂奏請以仲通舊院為軍營，乃移去真容自居之。

translations.literal: Yingyi, because he entered the abbey to burn incense, was pleased with its bamboo and trees, and memorialized to make Zhongtong's old compound a military camp; he then removed the true likeness and dwelt there himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyi visited the temple to burn incense, admired its grounds, and petitioned to turn Zhongtong's old compound into barracks, removing the portrait and taking up residence himself.

sentences.zh: 旰聞之，謂將士曰：「英乂反矣！

translations.literal: When Gan heard of it he said to the officers and soldiers: "Yingyi has rebelled!
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Gan told his officers, "Yingyi has committed treason!

sentences.zh: 不然，何得除毀玄宗真容而自居之？」

translations.literal: If not, how could he remove and destroy Xuanzong's true likeness and dwell there himself?"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise why would he destroy the emperor's portrait and live in that hall himself?"

sentences.zh: 乃率兵攻成都。

translations.literal: He then led troops to attack Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched on Chengdu at the head of his army.

sentences.zh: 英乂出兵於城西門，令柏茂琳為前軍，郭英幹為左軍，郭嘉琳為後軍，與旰戰。

translations.literal: Yingyi marched out at the city's west gate, appointing Bai Maolin as vanguard, Guo Yinggan as left wing, and Guo Jialin as rear guard, to fight Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyi led his forces out the west gate with Bai Maolin in the van, Guo Yinggan on the left, and Guo Jialin in the rear, to meet Gan in battle.

sentences.zh: 茂琳等軍累敗，軍人多投旰。

translations.literal: Maolin and the others' armies were repeatedly defeated, and many soldiers went over to Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Maolin's forces suffered repeated defeats, and soldiers defected to Gan in large numbers.

sentences.zh: 旰令降將統兵與英乂轉戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: Gan ordered surrendered generals to command troops and fight in rotation against Yingyi, defeating him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Gan put defecting officers in command and routed Yingyi in repeated engagements.

sentences.zh: 兵至子城，英乂單騎奔簡州，為普州刺史韓澄所殺。

translations.literal: When the troops reached the inner city, Yingyi fled alone on horseback to Jian Prefecture and was killed by Han Cheng, Prefect of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the fighting reached the inner citadel, Yingyi fled alone toward Jian Prefecture and was killed by Han Cheng of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 時邛、劍所在起兵相攻，劍南大亂。

translations.literal: At that time Qiong and Jian and other places all raised troops to attack one another, and Jiannan was in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Qiong, Jian, and other districts erupted in mutual warfare, plunging all Jiannan into chaos.

sentences.zh: 永泰二年二月，乃以黃門侍郎平章事杜鴻漸兼成都尹、山南西道劍南東川西川邛南等道副元帥、劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Yongtai, Du Hongjian, Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat and Participant in Court Deliberations, was made concurrently Governor of Chengdu, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Shannan West Circuit, Jiannan East Circuit, West Circuit, Qiong South, and related routes, and Military Commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 766 Du Hongjian, vice minister of the palace secretariat and chief councilor, was appointed governor of Chengdu, deputy commander-in-chief over the Shannan and Jiannan commands, and military commissioner of western Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸出駱谷，有謀者曰：「相公駐車閬州，遙制劍南，數移牒述英乂過失，言旰有方略；

translations.literal: As Hongjian came out through Luogu Pass, an adviser said: "Your Excellency should halt your carriage at Lang Prefecture and control Jiannan from afar, repeatedly sending documents describing Yingyi's faults and stating that Gan has strategy;
translations.idiomatic: As Hongjian emerged through Luogu Pass, an adviser urged him: "Hold at Lang Prefecture and govern Jiannan from a distance—send repeated dispatches detailing Yingyi's crimes and praising Gan's ability;

sentences.zh: 旰腹心攝諸州刺史者皆奏正之，令旰及將校不疑怨。

translations.literal: have Gan's trusted men who hold the various prefectures as acting prefects all memorialize to confirm them, so that Gan and the officers and soldiers harbor no suspicion or resentment.
translations.idiomatic: have Gan's loyalists holding prefectures confirm their appointments by memorial, so Gan and his officers feel no grievance.

sentences.zh: 然後與東川節度使張獻誠及諸賊帥合議，數出兵攻旰。

translations.literal: Then join in council with the Eastern Circuit Military Commissioner Zhang Xiancheng and the various rebel chiefs, and repeatedly send out troops to attack Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Then concert with eastern commissioner Zhang Xiancheng and other rebel leaders to attack Gan again and again.

sentences.zh: 既數道連兵，未經一年，兵勢減耗，旰窮，必束身歸朝。

translations.literal: Once several routes unite their armies, within less than a year military strength will be reduced and exhausted, Gan will be cornered, and he is certain to bind himself and return to the court.
translations.idiomatic: With several columns united, within a year his strength will be spent, Gan will be cornered, and he will surely surrender to the throne.

sentences.zh: 此上策也。」

translations.literal: This is the superior stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: That is the best course."

sentences.zh: 鴻漸畏懦，計疑未決。

translations.literal: Hongjian was timid and cowardly, and his plan wavered undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian was timid and could not settle on a plan.

sentences.zh: 會旰使至，卑辭厚禮，送繒錦數千匹。

translations.literal: Just then Gan's envoy arrived with humble words and generous gifts, presenting several thousand bolts of silk brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Then Gan's envoy arrived with humble words, lavish gifts, and several thousand bolts of brocade.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸貪其利，遂至成都，日與判官杜亞、楊炎將吏等高會縱觀，軍州政事悉委旰，乃連表聞薦。

translations.literal: Hongjian, greedy for the profit, then went on to Chengdu, daily holding lofty banquets and outings with his aides Du Ya, Yang Yan, officers, and clerks, entrusting all military and prefectural affairs to Gan, and repeatedly memorializing to report and recommend him.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for the gifts, Hongjian proceeded to Chengdu, spent his days feasting with aides Du Ya and Yang Yan and his staff, handed all civil and military affairs to Gan, and sent a stream of recommending memorials to court.

sentences.zh: 先時，張獻誠數與旰戰，獻誠屢敗，旌節皆為旰所奪。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Xiancheng had fought Gan several times; Xiancheng was repeatedly defeated and his banners and staffs were all seized by Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Xiancheng had fought Gan repeatedly, suffered defeat after defeat, and lost his command banners to him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因鴻漸之請，加成都尹，兼西山防禦使、西川節度行軍司馬，仍賜名曰寧。

translations.literal: The court, on Hongjian's request, added the title of Governor of Chengdu, concurrently Defender of the Western Hills and Campaigning Staff Officer of the West Circuit Military Commission, and moreover granted the name Ning.
translations.idiomatic: At Hongjian's urging the court made him governor of Chengdu, defender of the western hills, and campaigning deputy of the west circuit, and bestowed the name Ning.

sentences.zh: 大歷二年，鴻漸歸朝，遂授寧西川節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dali, when Hongjian returned to court, Ning was then appointed Military Commissioner of the West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongjian returned to the capital in 767, Ning was appointed full military commissioner of western Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 恃地險人富，乃厚斂財貨，結權貴，令弟寬留京師。

translations.literal: Relying on the land's strategic barriers and the people's wealth, he then heavily levied goods and wealth, formed ties with the powerful and noble, and had his younger brother Kuan remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Secure in a rich and defensible province, he levied heavy taxes, cultivated the powerful at court, and kept his brother Kuan in the capital.

sentences.zh: 元載及諸子有所欲，寬恣與之，故寬驟歷御史知雜事、御史中丞。

translations.literal: Whenever Yuan Zai and his sons desired something, Kuan gave freely, and therefore Kuan rapidly passed through Attending Censor in Charge of Miscellaneous Affairs to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Yuan Zai and his sons wanted, Kuan supplied without stint, and rose swiftly to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 寬兄審亦任郎中、諫議大夫、給事中。

translations.literal: Kuan's elder brother Shen also served as Langzhong, Remonstrance Grandee, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuan's older brother Shen likewise held the posts of Langzhong, Remonstrance Grandee, and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 寧在蜀十余年，地險兵強，肆侈窮欲，將吏妻妾，多為所淫汙，朝廷患之而不能詰。

translations.literal: Ning was in Shu for more than ten years; the land was rugged and its troops strong. He indulged extravagantly to the limit of desire, and many of the wives and concubines of his officers and officials were defiled by him. The court was troubled by this but could not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning spent over a decade in Shu, where the terrain was perilous and the army formidable. He gave free rein to luxury and every appetite, and many officers' and officials' wives and concubines fell victim to his abuses. The court resented this but had no power to call him to account.

sentences.zh: 累加尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively elevated to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 大歷十四年入朝，遷司空、平章事，兼山陵使，尋代喬琳為御史大夫、平章事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Dali he entered court, was transferred to Minister of Works and Co-Director of the Chancellery, and also served as Commissioner for Imperial Mausoleums. Shortly afterward he replaced Qiao Lin as Censor-in-Chief and Co-Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of the Dali reign he came to the capital, was appointed Minister of Works and Co-Director of the Chancellery, and concurrently made Commissioner for the Imperial Mausoleums. Before long he succeeded Qiao Lin as Censor-in-Chief and Co-Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 寧以為選擇御史當出大夫，不謀及宰相，乃奏請以李衡、於結等數人為御史。

translations.literal: Ning held that selecting censors should come from the Censor-in-Chief and need not involve the chancellors. He therefore memorialized requesting that Li Heng, Yu Jie, and several others be appointed censors.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning believed the appointment of censors was the Censor-in-Chief's prerogative and ought not to be discussed with the chancellors. He submitted a memorial proposing Li Heng, Yu Jie, and several others for the post of censor.

sentences.zh: 楊炎大怒，其狀遂寢。

translations.literal: Yang Yan was greatly enraged, and the memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan flew into a rage, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 炎又數讒毀劉晏，寧又求解之。

translations.literal: Yan again repeatedly slandered Liu Yan, and Ning again sought to intercede on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan again and again defamed Liu Yan, and Cui Ning once more pleaded for him.

sentences.zh: 寧既厚結元載已久，楊炎又出自載門，寧初附炎，炎因此大怒。

translations.literal: Ning had long been closely allied with Yuan Zai, and Yang Yan had also emerged from Zai's faction. Ning at first sided with Yan, and for this Yan was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning had for years cultivated a deep alliance with Yuan Zai, while Yang Yan himself had risen from Zai's circle. When Ning initially attached himself to Yan, Yan was all the more enraged.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，南蠻大下，與吐蕃三道合進。

translations.literal: That year, in the tenth month, the southern barbarians descended in force, advancing in concert with Tibet along three routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year the southern tribes launched a major invasion, joining with the Tibetans in a three-pronged advance.

sentences.zh: 一出茂州，過文川及灌口。

translations.literal: One column came out through Maozhou, passing Wenchuan and Guankou.
translations.idiomatic: One force issued from Maozhou, crossing Wenchuan and Guankou.

sentences.zh: 一出扶、文，過方維、白壩。

translations.literal: One came out through Fu and Wen, passing Fangwei and Baiba.
translations.idiomatic: Another came through Fu and Wen, passing Fangwei and Baiba.

sentences.zh: 一出黎壩、雅，過邛、郲。

translations.literal: One came out through Liba and Ya, passing Qiong and Lang.
translations.idiomatic: A third came through Liba and Ya, passing Qiong and Lang.

sentences.zh: 戎酋誡其眾曰：「吾要蜀川為東府，凡伎巧之工皆送邏娑，平歲賦一縑而已。」

translations.literal: The barbarian chieftain admonished his followers, saying, "I intend to make Shuchuan our eastern capital. All skilled craftsmen are to be sent to Luosuo, and in ordinary years the tribute shall be only one bolt of silk."
translations.idiomatic: The tribal leader warned his men: "I mean to make the Shu region our eastern domain. Every skilled artisan will be sent to Luosuo, and in normal years the levy will be no more than a single bolt of silk."

sentences.zh: 是蠻之入，連陷郡邑，士庶奔亡山谷。

translations.literal: When the barbarians entered, they successively captured prefectures and counties, and gentry and commoners fled into the mountains and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: As the invaders pushed in, they took one district after another, and officials and common people scattered into the hills and ravines.

sentences.zh: 屬寧在朝，軍中無帥，德宗促寧還鎮。

translations.literal: Ning happened to be at court, and with no commander in the army, Dezong urged Ning to return to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning was then at court, and with no general in command of the forces, Emperor Dezong pressed him to return to his post.

sentences.zh: 炎懼寧怨己，入蜀難制，謂德宗曰：「蜀川天下奧壤，自寧擅置其中，朝廷失其外府十四年矣。

translations.literal: Yan feared that Ning would resent him and that once back in Shu would be hard to control. He said to Dezong, "Shuchuan is the most vital territory under Heaven. Since Ning has held it at his own discretion, the court has lost its outer capital for fourteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan feared Cui Ning would bear a grudge and, once back in Shu, prove impossible to control. He told Dezong, "The Shu region is the richest strategic ground in the realm. Ever since Ning has ruled it as his private domain, the court has been without its outer capital for fourteen years.

sentences.zh: 今寧來朝，尚有全師守蜀。

translations.literal: Now that Ning has come to court, a full army still guards Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Even with Ning at court, Shu is still held by his intact army.

sentences.zh: 貨利之厚，適中奉給，貢賦所入，與無地同。

translations.literal: Its commercial profits are so abundant that they barely meet the central revenue needs, and the tribute and taxes it sends in are as if the land did not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Its wealth is so great that it barely suffices for the court's needs, yet the tribute and taxes it yields might as well belong to no territory at all.

sentences.zh: 始寧與諸將等夷，獨因叛亂得位，不敢自有，以恩柔煦育，威令不行。

translations.literal: At first Ning was equal among the generals and had seized power only through rebellion. He dared not act on his own authority, nurturing all with gentle kindness, so that authority and commands did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: At first Ning had stood on equal footing with the other generals and won his position only through rebellion. He did not dare assert himself, ruling instead through soft favors and indulgence, so that his authority never took hold.

sentences.zh: 今雖歸之，必無功，是徒遣也；

translations.literal: Even if he is sent back now, he will surely achieve nothing—it would be a wasted dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: If he is sent back now, he is bound to accomplish nothing; the expedition would be pointless.

sentences.zh: 若有功，義不可奪。

translations.literal: If he succeeds, it would be wrong to deprive him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if he succeeds, it would be unjust to strip him of command.

sentences.zh: 則西川之奧，敗固失之，勝亦非國家所有。

translations.literal: Then whether the vital core of western Shu is lost in defeat or won in victory, it will not belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In either case—defeat or victory—the heartland of western Shu would no longer truly be the state's to command.

sentences.zh: 陛下熟察。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should consider this carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should weigh this with care."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿策何從？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Which course do you advise?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What course do you recommend?"

sentences.zh: 炎曰：「請無歸寧。

translations.literal: Yan said, "I ask that Ning not be sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan replied, "I urge that Ning not be allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 今硃泚所部范陽勁兵，戍在近甸，促令與禁兵雜往，舉無不捷。

translations.literal: The elite troops of Fanyang under Zhu Ci's command are now garrisoned in the near provinces. Urge them to go mixed with the palace guards, and every campaign will succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The crack Fanyang troops under Zhu Ci are stationed close to the capital. Send them together with the palace guard, and no operation will fail.

sentences.zh: 因是役得置親兵內其腹中，蜀將必不敢動。

translations.literal: Through this campaign we can place trusted troops within their ranks, and the Shu generals will surely not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: In the process we can insert loyal troops into the army's core, and the Shu commanders will not dare stir.

sentences.zh: 然後換授他帥，以收其權，得千里肥饒之地，是因小禍受大福也。」

translations.literal: Then assign another commander to reclaim authority, gaining a thousand li of fertile land—turning a small misfortune into a great blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Then replace him with another commander, recover control, and gain a thousand li of rich territory—a small trouble exchanged for a great gain."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善」，即止寧不行。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Good," and stopped Ning from going.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said," and halted Cui Ning's departure.

sentences.zh: 乃發禁兵四千、范陽兵五千，赴援東川。

translations.literal: They then dispatched four thousand palace guards and five thousand Fanyang troops to aid eastern Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent four thousand palace guards and five thousand Fanyang soldiers to reinforce eastern Shu.

sentences.zh: 出軍自江油趣白壩，與山南兵合擊，蠻兵敗走。

translations.literal: The army set out from Jiangyou toward Baiba, joined with the Shannan forces in a combined attack, and the barbarian army was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The relief force marched from Jiangyou toward Baiba, united with the Shannan troops in a joint strike, and routed the invaders.

sentences.zh: 范陽軍又擊破於七盤，遂拔新城，戎、蠻大敗。

translations.literal: The Fanyang army routed them again at Qipan, then captured Xincheng, and the Rong and barbarians suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The Fanyang troops defeated them again at Qipan, took Xincheng, and the Rong and tribal forces were shattered.

sentences.zh: 凡斬馘六千，生擒六百，傷者殆半，饑寒隕於崖谷者八九萬。

translations.literal: In all, six thousand were beheaded, six hundred captured alive, nearly half were wounded, and eighty or ninety thousand perished from hunger and cold in the cliff ravines.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand heads were taken, six hundred prisoners captured, nearly half the enemy wounded, and eighty or ninety thousand more died of hunger and cold in the mountain gorges.

sentences.zh: 寧遂罷西川節度使，制授檢校司空、同中書門下平章事、御史大夫、京畿觀察使，兼靈州大都督、單於鎮北大都護、朔方節度等使，兼鄜坊丹延都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: Ning was then removed as military governor of western Shu and appointed Acting Minister of Works, Co-Director of the Chancellery, Censor-in-Chief, Capital Region Observation Commissioner, concurrently Grand Commander of Lingzhou, Commander-in-Chief of Danyu Zhenbei, Military Governor of Shuofang, and Consolidated Training and Observation Commissioner of Bian, Fang, Dan, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning was stripped of the western Shu governorship and appointed Acting Minister of Works, Co-Director of the Chancellery, Censor-in-Chief, and Capital Region Observation Commissioner, while also holding the titles of Grand Commander of Lingzhou, Commander-in-Chief of Danyu Zhenbei, Military Governor of Shuofang, and Consolidated Training and Observation Commissioner over Bian, Fang, Dan, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 托以重臣綏靖北邊，但令居鄜州。

translations.literal: Under the pretense of sending a senior minister to pacify the northern frontier, he was merely ordered to reside at Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the pretext of posting a high minister to settle the northern border, he was told only to take up residence at Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 雖以寧為節度，每道皆置留後，自得奏事，炎悉諷令伺寧過犯。

translations.literal: Although Ning held the governorship, a deputy was placed in each circuit who could memorialize directly to the throne, and Yan secretly instructed them all to watch for Ning's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ning remained nominal governor, Yang Yan installed a resident deputy in every circuit who could report directly to the throne, and secretly ordered them all to seek out Ning's missteps.

sentences.zh: 杜希全為靈州，王翃為振武，李建徽為鄜州，及戴休顏、杜從政、呂希倩等，皆炎署置也。

translations.literal: Du Xiquan at Lingzhou, Wang Hong at Zhenwu, Li Jianhui at Bianzhou, and Dai Xiuyan, Du Congzheng, Lü Xiqian, and others were all Yang Yan's appointees.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiquan in Lingzhou, Wang Hong in Zhenwu, Li Jianhui in Bianzhou, and Dai Xiuyan, Du Congzheng, Lü Xiqian, and the rest were all installed by Yang Yan.

sentences.zh: 寧巡邊至夏州，刺史呂希倩與寧同力招撫党項，歸降者甚多。

translations.literal: When Ning toured the frontier and reached Xiazhou, Prefect Lü Xiqian worked with him to win over the Tangut tribes, and many surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On a frontier tour Cui Ning reached Xiazhou, where Prefect Lü Xiqian joined him in winning over the Tangut peoples; a great many submitted.

sentences.zh: 炎惡之，因奏希倩撫綏之功，才堪委任。

translations.literal: Yan resented this and memorialized that Xiqian's achievements in pacification showed talent worthy of greater trust.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan took offense and submitted a memorial praising Xiqian's success in pacification and declaring him fit for higher responsibility.

sentences.zh: 召歸朝，除右僕射知省事，以神武將軍時常春代之。

translations.literal: Xiqian was recalled to court, appointed Right Vice Director overseeing Secretariat affairs, and General of the Divine Martial Forces Shi Changchun replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Xiqian was summoned back to court, made Right Vice Director with charge of Secretariat affairs, and replaced in Xiazhou by the Divine Martial General Shi Changchun.

sentences.zh: 硃泚之亂，上卒迫行幸，百僚諸王鮮有知者。

translations.literal: During Zhu Ci's rebellion the emperor was suddenly forced to flee on tour, and few among the hundred officials and princes knew beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rose in rebellion the emperor was abruptly driven to take flight, and scarcely any of the court officials or princes had forewarning.

sentences.zh: 寧後數日自賊中來，上初喜甚。

translations.literal: Several days later Ning came from the rebel-held zone, and at first the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Cui Ning arrived from the rebel-held city, and at first the emperor was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 寧私謂所親曰：「聖上聰明英邁，從善如轉規，但為盧杞所惑至此爾。」

translations.literal: Ning privately told his intimates, "His Majesty is wise and heroic and turns to good counsel as easily as a compass turns, but he has been misled by Lu Qi to reach this pass."
translations.idiomatic: In private Cui Ning told those close to him, "The Son of Heaven is brilliant and resolute, and accepts good advice as readily as a wheel turns—but Lu Qi has led him to this disaster."

sentences.zh: 杞聞之，潛與王翃圖議陷之。

translations.literal: Qi heard of it and secretly plotted with Wang Hong to entrap him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Qi learned of this, he secretly conspired with Wang Hong to frame him.

sentences.zh: 初，涇原兵作亂之夕，寧與翃及御史大夫於頎俱出延平門而西，數下馬便液，每下輒良久。

translations.literal: On the night the Jingyuan troops mutinied, Ning, Hong, and Censor-in-Chief Yu Yi all went out through Yanping Gate heading west. Several times they dismounted to urinate, and each stop lasted a long while.
translations.idiomatic: On the evening of the Jingyuan mutiny, Cui Ning, Wang Hong, and Censor-in-Chief Yu Yi all left through Yanping Gate and headed west. Again and again they dismounted to relieve themselves, lingering long each time.

sentences.zh: 翃等促之，不敢前。

translations.literal: Hong and the others urged him on, but he dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and the rest pressed him to move, yet he would not go forward.

sentences.zh: 又懼賊兵追及，翃乃大聲而言曰：「已至此，不必顧望。」

translations.literal: Fearing that rebel troops would overtake them, Hong then spoke loudly, saying, "We have come this far—there is no need to hesitate."
translations.idiomatic: Afraid the rebels would catch up, Wang Hong cried out, "We have come this far—there is no point in looking back."

sentences.zh: 至奉天，翃具以事聞。

translations.literal: When they reached Fengtian, Hong reported the whole affair to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After they reached Fengtian, Wang Hong laid the entire matter before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 會硃泚行反間，偽除柳渾宰相，署寧中書令。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci meanwhile ran a counterintelligence scheme, falsely appointing Liu Hun chancellor and naming Ning Zhongshu Ling.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Zhu Ci employed a ruse of disinformation, falsely appointing Liu Hun chancellor and naming Cui Ning Zhongshu Ling.

sentences.zh: 寧朔方掌書記康湛時為盩厔尉，翃逼湛作寧遺硃泚書，使寧無以自辯，翃遂獻之。

translations.literal: Kang Zhan, formerly Ning's chief secretary in Shuofang, was then magistrate of Zhouzhi. Hong forced Zhan to forge a letter from Ning to Zhu Ci so that Ning could not defend himself, and then submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Zhan, who had been Cui Ning's chief secretary in Shuofang and was then magistrate of Zhouzhi, was coerced by Wang Hong into forging a letter from Ning to Zhu Ci, leaving Ning unable to clear himself; Hong then presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 杞因誣奏曰：「崔寧初無葵藿向日之心，聞於城中與硃泚堅為盟約，所以後於百辟。

translations.literal: Qi thus falsely accused, saying, "Cui Ning from the first lacked the sunflower's devotion to the sun. It is said that within the city he bound himself in firm alliance with Zhu Ci, which is why he arrived after all the other officials.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi then lodged a false accusation: "Cui Ning never had a heart turned toward the throne like the sunflower toward the sun. I hear that inside the city he entered a firm pact with Zhu Ci—that is why he came days after the rest of the court.

sentences.zh: 今事果驗。

translations.literal: Now the matter has indeed been verified.
translations.idiomatic: Now the truth of it has been confirmed.

sentences.zh: 使兇渠外逼，奸臣內謀，則大事去矣。」

translations.literal: If the murderous rebel presses from without and treacherous ministers plot within, the great cause is lost."
translations.idiomatic: If a vicious enemy closes in from outside while traitors conspire within, the dynasty itself is finished."

sentences.zh: 因俯伏歔欷曰：「臣備位宰相，危不能持，顛不能扶，宜當萬死，伏待斧鉞。。」

translations.literal: He then prostrated himself, weeping, and said, "Your servant holds the place of chancellor yet could neither sustain the state in peril nor support it in collapse. I deserve ten thousand deaths and bow to await the axe."
translations.idiomatic: Then he threw himself down, weeping, and said, "I occupy the chancellor's seat yet could neither hold firm in crisis nor steady the throne in ruin. I deserve death ten thousand times over and submit myself to execution."

sentences.zh: 上命左右扶起之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered attendants to help him rise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commanded his attendants to lift him up.

sentences.zh: 既還，俄有中人引寧於幕後，二力士自後縊殺之，時年六十一。

translations.literal: Shortly after returning, eunuchs led Ning behind a screen, and two strongmen strangled him from behind. He was sixty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he withdrew, palace eunuchs summoned Cui Ning behind a curtain, where two brawny executioners garroted him from behind. He was sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 初，將誅寧，召至朝堂，云令江淮宣慰。

translations.literal: When they were about to execute Ning, he was summoned to the court hall on the pretext of appointing him Pacification Commissioner for Jianghuai.
translations.idiomatic: Before Cui Ning was to be killed, he was called to the audience hall under the pretense of sending him as Pacification Commissioner to Jianghuai.

sentences.zh: 尋命翰林學士陸贄草誅寧制；

translations.literal: Soon afterward they ordered Hanlin Academician Lu Zhi to draft the edict condemning Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, the emperor ordered the Hanlin Academician Lu Zhi to compose the decree ordering Ning's execution.

sentences.zh: 贄求寧與泚書，將以狀生之。

translations.literal: Zhi requested Ning's letter to Ci, intending to verify the accusation by the document itself.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi asked to see Ning's letter to Zhu Ci, hoping to test the charge against the document itself.

sentences.zh: 復亂言云，其書已失。

translations.literal: Ning then spoke confusedly, saying the letter was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning answered incoherently that the letter was already gone.

sentences.zh: 寧既得罪，籍沒其家，中外稱其冤，乃赦其家，歸其資產。

translations.literal: After Ning was condemned, his household was confiscated. Inside and outside the court called it an injustice, and the throne then pardoned his family and restored their property.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cui Ning was condemned, his estate was seized. Court and country alike called it a miscarriage of justice, and the throne eventually pardoned his family and returned their assets.

sentences.zh: 貞元十二年六月，寧故將、夏、綏、銀節度使韓潭奏請以新加禮部尚書恩制以雪寧之罪。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year of Zhenyuan, Han Tan, Ning's former subordinate and military governor of Xia, Sui, and Yin, memorialized requesting that the newly granted Minister of Rites title and favor edict be used to clear Ning's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twelfth year of Zhenyuan, Han Tan—once Cui Ning's officer and now military governor of Xia, Sui, and Yin—petitioned that the recent honorific appointment as Minister of Rites be applied to exonerate Ning.

sentences.zh: 詔從之，任其家收葬。

translations.literal: An edict approved the request and permitted his family to retrieve the body for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented and allowed the family to recover the body for burial.

sentences.zh: 初，寧入朝，留弟寬守成都。

translations.literal: When Ning first entered court, he left his brother Kuan to guard Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Ning first came to the capital, he left his brother Cui Kuan to hold Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 瀘州楊子琳乘間以精騎數千突入成都，據城守之。

translations.literal: Yang Zilin of Luzhou seized the moment with several thousand elite cavalry, burst into Chengdu, and held the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zilin of Luzhou took advantage of the opening, leading several thousand crack horsemen in a sudden rush into Chengdu, which he then occupied.

sentences.zh: 寬屢戰力屈，子琳威聲頗盛。

translations.literal: Kuan fought repeatedly but was worn down, and Zilin's reputation grew formidable.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuan fought again and again until his strength gave out, while Yang Zilin's prestige swelled.

sentences.zh: 寧妾任氏魁偉果幹，乃出其家財十萬募勇士，信宿間得千人，設隊伍將校，手自麾兵，以逼子琳。

translations.literal: Ning's concubine Lady Ren was tall, bold, and capable. She spent one hundred thousand from the family fortune to recruit warriors; within two days she gathered a thousand men, organized ranks and officers, and personally commanded the troops to press Zilin.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning's concubine, Lady Ren, was imposing in stature and resolute in action. She poured one hundred thousand coins of family wealth into recruiting fighters; within two nights she raised a thousand men, formed companies and appointed officers, and herself led the force against Yang Zilin.

sentences.zh: 子琳懼，城內糧盡，乃拔城自潰。

translations.literal: Zilin feared the attack; grain in the city ran out, and he abandoned the city in self-rout.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zilin grew afraid. With provisions exhausted inside the walls, he broke camp and fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 子琳素有妖術，其夕致大雨，引舟至庭除，登之而遁。

translations.literal: Zilin had long practiced occult arts. That evening he brought a great rain, drew a boat to the courtyard, boarded it, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zilin was known for sorcery. That night he summoned a torrential rain, had a boat brought into the courtyard, stepped aboard, and vanished.

sentences.zh: 崔密、密子崔繪

translations.literal: Cui Mi; Mi's son Cui Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Mi, and his son Cui Hui.

sentences.zh: 寧季弟密，密子繪，父子皆以文雅稱，歷使府從事。

translations.literal: Ning's younger brother Mi; Mi's son Hui—father and son were both known for literary refinement and served as staff members in military commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning's younger brother Mi and Mi's son Hui were both celebrated for literary elegance and served as aides in various military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 繪生四子：蠡、黯、確、顏，皆以進士擢第。

translations.literal: Hui had four sons: Li, An, Que, and Yan—all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hui fathered four sons—Li, An, Que, and Yan—each of whom earned the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 蠡，字越卿，元和五年擢第，累辟使府。

translations.literal: Li, styled Yueqing, passed in the fifth year of Yuanhe and was repeatedly recruited to commission staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Li, courtesy name Yueqing, passed the examinations in the fifth year of Yuanhe and was repeatedly invited into service on military staffs.

sentences.zh: 寶歷中，入朝監察御史。

translations.literal: During Baoli he entered court as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoli reign he entered court as Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 大和初，為侍御史，三遷戶部郎中，出為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Dahe he was Attending Censor, was promoted three times to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and was then sent out as Prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Dahe reign he served as Attending Censor, rose through three promotions to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and was then appointed Prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 開成初，以司勛郎中征，尋以本官知制誥。

translations.literal: Early in Kaicheng he was recalled as Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and soon held that office while drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaicheng he was recalled as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and soon added the duty of drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 明年，正拜舍人。

translations.literal: The next year he was formally appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received formal appointment as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 三年，權知禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: In the third year he served as acting director of the Ministry of Rites overseeing the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made acting head of the Ministry of Rites with charge over the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜禮部侍郎，轉戶部。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, then transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, then moved to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 上疏論國忌日設僧齋，百官行香，事無經據。

translations.literal: He memorialized that on national mourning days setting Buddhist vegetarian feasts and having the hundred officials burn incense lacked canonical basis.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial arguing that holding Buddhist vegetarian feasts in temples on state mourning days and requiring all officials to burn incense had no foundation in classical ritual.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕以郊廟之禮，嚴奉祖宗，備物盡誠，庶幾昭格。

translations.literal: The edict said, "We, with the rites of suburban and ancestral temples, reverently serve our forebears, providing every offering in full sincerity, hoping they may clearly descend.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "We observe the rites of the suburban altars and ancestral temples, serving our forebears with strict devotion, offering every requisite gift in utmost sincerity, that their spirits may be clearly received.

sentences.zh: 恭惟忌日之感，所謂終身之憂。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering the grief of a death anniversary—what is called a lifetime's sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: With reverence we regard the feeling of a mourning anniversary—what the sages called a sorrow lasting one's whole life.

sentences.zh: 而近代以來，歸依釋、老，征二教以設食，會百辟以行香。

translations.literal: Yet in recent times people have turned to Buddhism and Daoism, summoning both teachings to set out food and gathering the hundred ministers to burn incense.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in recent generations people have looked to Buddhism and Daoism, invoking both faiths to lay out offerings and assembling the whole court to burn incense.

sentences.zh: 將以有助聖靈，冥資福祚。

translations.literal: Intending thereby to aid the imperial souls and silently confer blessing and fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was to assist the imperial dead in the unseen realm and quietly accumulate merit and blessing.

sentences.zh: 有異皇王之術，頗乖教義之宗。

translations.literal: This differs from the methods of emperors and kings and departs considerably from the root of teaching and principle.
translations.idiomatic: Such practice diverges from the way of true kingship and strays far from the foundations of proper doctrine.

sentences.zh: 昨得崔蠡奏論，遂遣討尋本末，禮文令式，曾不該明，習俗因循，雅當整革。

translations.literal: Yesterday We received Cui Li's memorial on this and sent inquiry into origins and ends. Ceremonial texts and regulations never clearly covered it; custom has merely followed precedent—it should rightly be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday We received Cui Li's memorial and ordered an investigation of its origins. Neither ritual codes nor administrative regulations ever clearly prescribed it; the custom has simply lingered by inertia—and ought now to be corrected.

sentences.zh: 其兩京、天下州府，以國忌日為寺觀設齋焚香，從今已後，並宜停罷。」

translations.literal: In both capitals and all prefectures under Heaven, setting vegetarian feasts and burning incense at temples and abbeys on national mourning days—all shall cease from this day forward."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, in both capitals and every prefecture in the realm, the practice of holding temple feasts and burning incense on state mourning days is abolished entirely."

sentences.zh: 蠡尋為華州刺史、鎮國軍等使，再歷方鎮。

translations.literal: Li soon became Prefect of Huazhou and commissioner of the Zhenguo Army, and served twice in regional commands.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Li was soon made Prefect of Huazhou and commissioner of the Zhenguo Army, and twice held frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 子蕘。

translations.literal: His son was Rao.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Cui Rao.

sentences.zh: 蕘，字野夫。

translations.literal: Rao, styled Yefu.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Rao, courtesy name Yefu.

sentences.zh: 大中二年，擢進士第，累官至尚書郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong he passed the jinshi examination and rose to Court Gentleman of the Secretariat and edict drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dazhong he earned the jinshi degree and advanced to Secretariat Gentleman and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 正拜中書舍人、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was formally appointed Secretariat Drafter and Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He received formal appointment as Secretariat Drafter and Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，自尚書右丞遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: During Qianfu he moved from Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianfu reign he was transferred from Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 蕘美文詞，善談論，而馭事簡率，銓管非所長。

translations.literal: Rao excelled in literary composition and was skilled in discussion, but managed affairs with casual brevity—not his strength was personnel evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Rao wrote elegantly and debated well, but handled office business with loose informality; managing appointments was not his forte.

sentences.zh: 出為陜州觀察使，以器韻自高，不屑細故，權移仆下。

translations.literal: Sent out as Observation Commissioner of Shanzhou, he held himself loftily by bearing and tone, disdaining small matters, and authority passed to subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: When he was sent out as Observation Commissioner of Shanzhou, he carried himself with lofty airs, scorned petty affairs, and let power slip down to his underlings.

sentences.zh: 時河南寇盜蜂起，王仙芝亂漢南，朝綱不振，而蕘自恃清貴，不恤人之疾苦。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose across Henan like hornets; Wang Xianzhi ravaged southern Han; court discipline faltered—yet Rao relied on his pure eminence and did not care for people's suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits swarmed across Henan like wasps; Wang Xianzhi wreaked havoc in southern Han; the court's authority crumbled—yet Cui Rao, trusting in his own refined rank, paid no heed to the people's hardship.

sentences.zh: 百姓訴旱，蕘指庭樹曰：「此尚有葉，何旱之有？」

translations.literal: When common people complained of drought, Rao pointed at a courtyard tree and said, "It still has leaves—how can there be drought?"
translations.idiomatic: When villagers came pleading about drought, Cui Rao pointed to a tree in the courtyard and said, "See—it still has leaves. What drought is there?"

sentences.zh: 乃笞之，吏民結怨。

translations.literal: He had them beaten, and officials and people nursed grievances.
translations.idiomatic: He had them flogged, and officials and commoners alike seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 既而為軍人所逐，饑渴甚，投民舍求水，民以溺飲之。

translations.literal: Before long soldiers drove him out. Tormented by hunger and thirst, he entered a commoner's house begging for water, and the people gave him urine to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his own troops expelled him. Half dead from hunger and thirst, he stumbled into a peasant home to beg for water—and the people gave him urine to drink.

sentences.zh: 初為軍人所俘，翦其髭發，拜而獲免。

translations.literal: At first he was captured by soldiers; they cut off his beard and hair; he bowed and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When first taken by his troops he was held captive; they shaved his beard and queue, but he bowed in submission and was allowed to go.

sentences.zh: 以失守貶端州司馬，復入為左散騎常侍，卒。

translations.literal: For losing his post he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Duanzhou; he later re-entered court as Left Regular Attendant of the Imperial Insignia and died.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to vice prefect of Duanzhou for failing to hold his command, he later returned to court as Left Regular Attendant of the Imperial Insignia and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子居敬、居儉。

translations.literal: His sons were Jujing and Jujian.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Jujing and Jujian.

sentences.zh: 居敬終尚書郎，居儉中興終戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Jujing ended as a Secretariat Director; Jujian, in the Zhongxing era, ended as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Jujing rose no higher than a secretariat director; Jujian eventually served as Minister of Revenue, reaching that post during the Zhongxing era.

sentences.zh: 黯，字直卿，大和二年，進士擢第。

translations.literal: An, styled Zhiqing—in the second year of Dahe passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Cui An, courtesy name Zhiqing, passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Dahe (828).

sentences.zh: 開成初，為青州從事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng he served as staff officer of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaicheng reign he served as staff officer of Qing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為監察御史，奏郊廟祭器不虔，請敕有司。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Investigating Censor, memorialized that suburban and temple sacrificial vessels were treated without reverence, and requested that the responsible agencies be commanded.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital as Investigating Censor, he reported that sacrificial vessels at the suburban altars and ancestral temples were not being maintained with due reverence, and asked that the responsible agencies be ordered to correct this.

sentences.zh: 文宗謂宰臣曰：「宗廟之事，朕合親奉其禮，但以千乘萬騎，動費國用，每有司行事之日，被衣冠坐以俟旦。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong said to the chief ministers: "In ancestral temple affairs I ought personally to perform the rites, but with thousands of chariots and myriad horsemen the cost to the treasury is great; on each day the officials perform the ceremony, I don robes and cap and sit awaiting dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong told his chief ministers, "In ancestral temple matters I ought to perform the rites myself, but a procession of thousands of chariots and horsemen drains the treasury. On each day the officials carry out the ceremony I don ceremonial robes and hat and sit waiting for dawn.

sentences.zh: 比聞主者不虔，祭器勞敝，非事神蠲潔之義。

translations.literal: Recently I heard the officiants are irreverent and the sacrificial vessels worn and damaged—not the meaning of serving the spirits with purification and cleanliness.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I hear the officiants have grown careless and the sacrificial vessels worn and neglected—hardly the spirit of serving the gods in purity and cleanliness.

sentences.zh: 卿宜嚴敕有司，道吾此意。」

translations.literal: You should strictly command the responsible agencies and convey My intention."
translations.idiomatic: You should sternly instruct the responsible agencies and make My intention known."

sentences.zh: 黯具條奏以聞。

translations.literal: An fully itemized a memorial to report.
translations.idiomatic: Cui An submitted a detailed memorial reporting back.

sentences.zh: 尋遷員外郎。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Supernumerary Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Supernumerary Director.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: During Huichang he served as Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huichang reign he served as Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 崔確、崔顏

translations.literal: Cui Que and Cui Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Que and Cui Yan.

sentences.zh: 確，字嶽卿，顏，字希卿，位皆至尚書郎。

translations.literal: Que, styled Yueqing, and Yan, styled Xiqing—both reached the rank of Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: Que, courtesy name Yueqing, and Yan, courtesy name Xiqing, both attained the rank of secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 嚴震，字遐聞，梓州鹽亭人。

translations.literal: Yan Zhen, styled Xiawen, was a native of Yanting in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhen, courtesy name Xiawen, was a native of Yanting in Zizhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世為田家，以財雄於鄉里。

translations.literal: For generations a farming household, distinguished by wealth in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: His family were farmers for generations, but their wealth made them the most powerful household in the district.

sentences.zh: 至德、乾元已後，震屢出家財以助邊軍，授州長史、王府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: After the Zhide and Qianyuan eras Yan Zhen repeatedly contributed family wealth to aid the frontier armies and was appointed chief secretary of a prefecture and advisory officer on a princely staff.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhide and Qianyuan eras Yan Zhen repeatedly contributed his family fortune to support the border armies and was appointed chief secretary of a prefecture and advisory officer on a princely staff.

sentences.zh: 東川節度判官韋收薦震才用於節度使嚴武，遂授合州長史。
