translations.literal: Wei Shou, aide to the Dongchuan military commission, recommended Yan Zhen's talents to the military commissioner Yan Wu, who then appointed him chief secretary of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou, aide to the Dongchuan military commission, recommended Yan Zhen's abilities to the military commissioner Yan Wu, who then appointed him chief secretary of He prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及嚴武移西川，署為押衙，改恆王府司馬。

translations.literal: When Yan Wu transferred to Xichuan he appointed Yan Zhen guard officer of the headquarters, then made him vice prefect on the staff of the Prince of Heng.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Wu moved to Xichuan command, he appointed Yan Zhen guard officer of the headquarters, then made him vice prefect on the staff of the Prince of Heng.

sentences.zh: 嚴武以宗姓之故，軍府之事多以委之，又歷試衛尉、太常少卿。

translations.literal: Because they shared the same surname, Yan Wu entrusted Yan Zhen with much of the military headquarters' business; he also served in succession as Vice Minister of the Guard and Vice Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Because they shared the same surname, Yan Wu entrusted Yan Zhen with much of the military headquarters' business; he also served in succession as Vice Minister of the Guard and Vice Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 嚴武卒，乃罷歸。

translations.literal: When Yan Wu died he was relieved of office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Wu died he was relieved of office and returned home.

sentences.zh: 東川節度使又奏為渝州刺史，以疾免。

translations.literal: The Dongchuan military commissioner again recommended him as prefect of Yuzhou, but illness prevented him from taking up the post.
translations.idiomatic: The Dongchuan military commissioner again recommended him as prefect of Yu prefecture, but illness prevented him from taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 山南西道節度使又奏為鳳州刺史，加侍御史，丁母憂罷。

translations.literal: The Shannan West circuit military commissioner next recommended him as prefect of Fengzhou and Attending Censor; he resigned when his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: The Shannan West circuit military commissioner next recommended him as prefect of Feng prefecture and Attending Censor; he resigned when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 起復本官，仍充興、鳳兩州團練使，累加開府儀同三司、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning to his former posts, he was also made regimental commissioner of Xing and Feng prefectures, and eventually received the honorary title of Grand General of the Palace Guards with rank equal to the Three Dukes, concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning to his former posts, he was also made regimental commissioner of Xing and Feng prefectures, and eventually received the honorary title of Grand General of the Palace Guards with rank equal to the Three Dukes, concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 為政清嚴，興利除害，遠近稱美。

translations.literal: His governance was pure and strict; he promoted benefits and removed harm, and was praised near and far.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with austere integrity, promoted public good and cleared away abuses, and won praise throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 建中初，司勛郎中韋楨為山、劍黜陟使，薦震理行為山南第一，特賜上下考，封鄖國公。

translations.literal: Early in Jianzhong, Director of Merits Wei Zhen served as commissioner for evaluating officials in the mountain and sword circuits; he rated Yan Zhen's governance the best in Shannan, the emperor granted him the highest personnel evaluation, and he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong, Director of Merits Wei Zhen served as commissioner for evaluating officials in the mountain and sword circuits; he rated Yan Zhen's governance the best in Shannan, the emperor granted him the highest personnel evaluation, and he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 在鳳州十四年，能政不渝。

translations.literal: He served at Fengzhou for fourteen years, and his capable governance never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: He served at Feng prefecture for fourteen years, and his capable administration never slackened.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，代賈耽為梁州刺史、兼御史大夫、山南西道節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong he succeeded Jia Dan as prefect of Liangzhou, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and military and observation commissioner of Shannan West circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianzhong he succeeded Jia Dan as prefect of Liang prefecture, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and military and observation commissioner of Shannan West circuit.

sentences.zh: 及硃泚竊據京城，李懷光頓軍咸陽，又與之連結。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci seized the capital Li Huaiguang was encamped at Xianyang and was in league with him as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci seized the capital Li Huaiguang was encamped at Xianyang and was in league with him as well.

sentences.zh: 泚令腹心穆庭光、宋瑗等賫白書誘震同叛，震集眾斬庭光等。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci sent his trusted agents Mu Tingguang and Song Yuan and others with personal letters urging Yan Zhen to join the rebellion; Yan Zhen assembled his forces and had Tingguang and the others executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci sent his trusted agents Mu Tingguang and Song Yuan and others with personal letters urging Yan Zhen to join the rebellion; Yan Zhen assembled his forces and had Tingguang and the others executed.

sentences.zh: 時李懷光連賊，德宗欲移幸山南。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang was in league with the rebels, and Emperor Dezong planned to move the court into Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang was in league with the rebels, and Emperor Dezong planned to move the court into Shannan.

sentences.zh: 震既聞順動，遣吏馳表往奉天迎駕，仍令大將張用誠領兵五千至盩厔已東迎護，上聞之喜。

translations.literal: As soon as Yan Zhen learned of the emperor's movement toward loyal territory, he dispatched clerks with an urgent memorial to Fengtian to welcome the imperial procession, and ordered his great general Zhang Yongcheng to lead five thousand men east of Zhouzhi to receive and escort the court; the emperor was overjoyed when he heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Yan Zhen learned of the emperor's movement toward loyal territory, he dispatched clerks with an urgent memorial to Fengtian to welcome the imperial procession, and ordered his great general Zhang Yongcheng to lead five thousand men east of Zhouzhi to receive and escort the court; the emperor was overjoyed when he heard of it.

sentences.zh: 既而用誠為賊所誘，欲謀背逆，朝廷憂之。

translations.literal: Before long Zhang Yongcheng was won over by the rebels and planned to turn traitor, filling the court with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhang Yongcheng was won over by the rebels and planned to turn traitor, filling the court with alarm.

sentences.zh: 會震又遣牙將馬勛奉表迎候，上臨軒召勛與之語，勛對曰：「臣請計日至山南取節度使符召用誠，即不受召，臣當斬其首以復。」

translations.literal: Then Yan Zhen sent his adjutant Ma Xun with another memorial to attend the emperor; the emperor received him in audience at the palace steps. Ma Xun answered, "Allow me to set a date to reach Shannan, take the military commissioner's seal of authority and summon Zhang Yongcheng—if he refuses the summons, I shall strike off his head and report back."
translations.idiomatic: Then Yan Zhen sent his adjutant Ma Xun with another memorial to attend the emperor; the emperor received him in audience at the palace steps. Ma Xun answered, "Allow me to set a date to reach Shannan, take the military commissioner's seal of authority and summon Zhang Yongcheng—if he refuses the summons, I shall strike off his head and report back."

sentences.zh: 上喜曰：「卿何日當至？」

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and asked, "On what day will you arrive?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and asked, "On what day will you arrive?"

sentences.zh: 勛克日時而奏，帝勉勞之。

translations.literal: Ma Xun fixed a day and hour and submitted his answer, and the emperor commended and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xun fixed a day and hour and submitted his answer, and the emperor commended and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 勛既得震符，乃請壯丁五人偕行。

translations.literal: Once Ma Xun had Yan Zhen's seal of authority, he asked for five strong men to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ma Xun had Yan Zhen's seal of authority, he asked for five strong men to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 既出駱谷，用誠以勛未知其謀，乃以數百騎迎勛，勛與俱之傳舍，用誠左右森然。

translations.literal: Once they had passed through Luogu Pass, Zhang Yongcheng, believing Ma Xun unaware of his plot, rode out with several hundred cavalry to meet him. Ma Xun went with him to a relay station where Yongcheng's men stood ranks deep on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had passed through Luogu Pass, Zhang Yongcheng, believing Ma Xun unaware of his plot, rode out with several hundred cavalry to meet him. Ma Xun went with him to a relay station where Yongcheng's men stood ranks deep on every side.

sentences.zh: 勛先聚草發火於驛外，軍士爭附火。

translations.literal: Ma Xun first piled grass and set it ablaze outside the relay station, and the soldiers all rushed to warm themselves at the fire.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xun first piled grass and set it ablaze outside the relay station, and the soldiers all rushed to warm themselves at the fire.

sentences.zh: 勛乃從容出懷中符示之曰：「大夫召君。」

translations.literal: Then Ma Xun calmly produced the seal from his robe and showed it, saying, "The commissioner summons you."
translations.idiomatic: Then Ma Xun calmly produced the seal from his robe and showed it, saying, "The commissioner summons you."

sentences.zh: 用誠惶懼起走，壯士自背束手而擒之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yongcheng leapt up in panic and tried to flee, but the strong men seized him from behind with his arms pinned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongcheng leapt up in panic and tried to flee, but the strong men seized him from behind with his arms pinned.

sentences.zh: 不虞用誠子居後，引刀斫勛，勛左右遽承其臂，刀下不甚，微傷勛首。

translations.literal: Unexpectedly Zhang Yongcheng's son was lurking behind and struck at Ma Xun with a blade; Ma Xun's men instantly caught the arm, so the blow was not heavy—a glancing cut to Ma Xun's head.
translations.idiomatic: Unexpectedly Zhang Yongcheng's son was lurking behind and struck at Ma Xun with a blade; Ma Xun's men instantly caught the arm, so the blow was not heavy—a glancing cut to Ma Xun's head.

sentences.zh: 遂格殺其子，而仆用誠於地。

translations.literal: They thereupon beat the son to death and threw Zhang Yongcheng to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon beat the son to death and threw Zhang Yongcheng to the ground.

sentences.zh: 壯士跨其腹，以刃擬其喉曰：「出聲即死！」

translations.literal: A strong man straddled his belly and pressed a blade to his throat, saying, "One sound and you die!"
translations.idiomatic: A strong man straddled his belly and pressed a blade to his throat, saying, "One sound and you die!"

sentences.zh: 勛即其營，軍士已被甲執兵矣。

translations.literal: Ma Xun marched straight into their camp—the soldiers were already armored and armed.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xun marched straight into their camp—the soldiers were already armored and armed.

sentences.zh: 勛大言曰：「汝等父母妻子皆在梁州，一朝棄之，欲從用誠反逆，有何利也？

translations.literal: Ma Xun shouted, "Your parents, wives, and children are all at Liangzhou—will you cast them aside in a morning to follow Zhang Yongcheng in treason? What profit is there?
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xun shouted, "Your parents, wives, and children are all at Liang prefecture—will you cast them aside in a morning to follow Zhang Yongcheng in treason? What good can that do you?

sentences.zh: 但滅汝族耳！

translations.literal: You will only bring destruction on your whole families!
translations.idiomatic: You will only bring destruction on your whole families!

sentences.zh: 大夫使我取張用誠，不問汝輩，欲何為乎？」

translations.literal: The commissioner sent me only to take Zhang Yongcheng, not to question the rest of you—what do you intend?"
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner sent me only to take Zhang Yongcheng, not to question the rest of you—what do you mean to do?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆詟服。

translations.literal: The men all cowered into submission.
translations.idiomatic: The men all cowered into submission.

sentences.zh: 於是縛用誠送州，震杖殺之，拔其副將，使率其眾迎駕。

translations.literal: They bound Zhang Yongcheng and sent him to the prefectural seat; Yan Zhen had him beaten to death with the staff, promoted a deputy in his place, and ordered him to lead the troops to welcome the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They bound Zhang Yongcheng and sent him to the prefectural seat; Yan Zhen had him beaten to death with the staff, promoted a deputy in his place, and ordered him to lead the troops to welcome the emperor.

sentences.zh: 勛以藥封首馳赴行在，愆約半日，上頗憂之，及勛至，上喜動顏色。

translations.literal: Ma Xun dressed his wound and galloped to the emperor's camp. He was half a day late on his promise, and the emperor grew anxious—but when Ma Xun arrived the emperor's face lit with joy.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xun dressed his wound and galloped to the emperor's camp. He was half a day late on his promise, and the emperor grew anxious—but when Ma Xun arrived the emperor's face lit with joy.

sentences.zh: 翌日，車駕發奉天，及入駱谷，李懷光遣數百騎來襲，賴山南兵擊之而退，輿駕無警急之患。

translations.literal: The next day the imperial procession left Fengtian. As they entered Luogu Pass Li Huaiguang sent several hundred cavalry to attack, but Shannan troops drove them back and the imperial train met with no serious danger.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the imperial procession left Fengtian. As they entered Luogu Pass Li Huaiguang sent several hundred cavalry to attack, but Shannan troops drove them back and the imperial train met with no serious danger.

sentences.zh: 尋加震檢校戶部尚書，賜實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Yan Zhen was soon given the additional title of acting Minister of Revenue and granted an actual fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhen was soon given the additional title of acting Minister of Revenue and granted an actual fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 三月，德宗至梁州。

translations.literal: In the third month Emperor Dezong reached Liang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Emperor Dezong reached Liang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 山南地貧，糧食難給，宰臣議請幸成都府。

translations.literal: Shannan was poor and grain scarce, and the chief ministers debated urging the emperor to move on to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shannan was poor and grain scarce, and the chief ministers debated urging the emperor to move on to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 震奏曰：「山南地接京畿，李晟方圖收復，藉六軍聲援。

translations.literal: Yan Zhen memorialized, "Shannan adjoins the capital region. Li Sheng is working to recover the city and needs the moral support of the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhen memorialized, "Shannan adjoins the capital region. Li Sheng is working to recover the city and needs the moral support of the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 如幸西川，則晟未見收復之期也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty proceeds to Xichuan, Li Sheng will have no hope of a date for recovery.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty proceeds to Xichuan, Li Sheng will have no hope of a date for recovery.

sentences.zh: 幸陛下徐思其宜。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will weigh this carefully."
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will weigh this carefully."

sentences.zh: 議未決，李晟表至，請車駕駐蹕梁、洋，以圖收復，群議乃止。

translations.literal: Before a decision was made, Li Sheng's memorial arrived asking that the court remain at Liang and Yang prefectures while planning recovery, and the discussion ended.
translations.idiomatic: Before a decision was made, Li Sheng's memorial arrived asking that the court remain at Liang and Yang prefectures while planning recovery, and the discussion ended.

sentences.zh: 梁、漢之間，刀耕火耨，民以采穭為事，雖節察十五郡，而賦額不敵中原三數縣。

translations.literal: Between Liang and Han the people burned clearings for fields and lived by gathering wild grain; though the circuit encompassed fifteen prefectures, its tax quota was less than that of a handful of counties in the central plain.
translations.idiomatic: Between Liang and Han the people burned clearings for fields and lived by gathering wild grain; though the circuit encompassed fifteen prefectures, its tax quota was less than that of a handful of counties in the central plain.

sentences.zh: 自安、史之後，多為山賊剽掠，戶口流散大半。

translations.literal: Since the An Lushan rebellion mountain bandits had ravaged the region and more than half the population had dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the An Lushan rebellion mountain bandits had ravaged the region and more than half the population had dispersed.

sentences.zh: 洎六師駐蹕，震設法勸課，鳩聚財賦，以給行在，民不至煩，供億無闕。

translations.literal: When the imperial army arrived Yan Zhen devised methods to encourage production and gathered revenue to supply the mobile court without overburdening the people, and provisions never ran short.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army arrived Yan Zhen devised methods to encourage production and gathered revenue to supply the mobile court without overburdening the people, and provisions never ran short.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，收復京城，車駕將還京師，進位檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: That June, when the capital was recovered and the emperor prepared to return, Yan Zhen was promoted to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That June, when the capital was recovered and the emperor prepared to return, Yan Zhen was promoted to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕遭罹寇難，播越梁、岷，蒸庶煩於供億，武旅勤於扞衛。

translations.literal: The edict read, "We have suffered rebellion and been driven into Liang and Min; the people have been burdened with provisioning and the troops have labored in our defense.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "We have suffered rebellion and been driven into Liang and Min; the people have been burdened with provisioning and the troops have labored in our defense.

sentences.zh: 凡百執事，各奉厥司，眷於是邦，復我興運，宜加崇大，以示將來。

translations.literal: Every official has done his duty. Because this land has sheltered us and helped restore the dynasty's fortunes, it should be greatly honored as a sign to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Every official has done his duty. Because this land has sheltered us and helped restore the dynasty's fortunes, it should be greatly honored as a sign to posterity.

sentences.zh: 宜改梁州為興元府，官名品制，同京兆、河南府；

translations.literal: Liang prefecture shall be renamed Xingyuan Prefecture, with official titles and institutions equal to those of the capitals Jingzhao and Henan;
translations.idiomatic: Liang prefecture shall be renamed Xingyuan Prefecture, with official titles and institutions equal to those of the capitals Jingzhao and Henan;

sentences.zh: 鄭縣升為赤，諸縣升為畿。

translations.literal: Zheng county shall be raised to imperial status, and all other counties to metropolitan status.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng county shall be raised to imperial status, and all other counties to metropolitan status.

sentences.zh: 見任州縣官，考滿日放選，百姓給復一年。

translations.literal: Current prefectural and county officials shall be released for new appointments when their evaluations are complete, and the people granted one year's tax remission.
translations.idiomatic: Current prefectural and county officials shall be released for new appointments when their evaluations are complete, and the people granted one year's tax remission.

sentences.zh: 洋州宜升為望，見任州縣官，考滿減兩選。

translations.literal: Yang prefecture shall be raised to distinguished status; incumbent officials there shall advance two selection cycles early upon completing their evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Yang prefecture shall be raised to distinguished status; incumbent officials there shall advance two selection cycles early upon completing their evaluations.

sentences.zh: 山南西道將士，並與甄敘。」

translations.literal: All officers and soldiers of Shannan West circuit shall receive evaluation for promotion and rewards."
translations.idiomatic: All officers and soldiers of Shannan West circuit shall receive evaluation for promotion and rewards."

sentences.zh: 以震為興元尹，賜實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Yan Zhen was appointed Governor of Xingyuan and granted an actual fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhen was appointed Governor of Xingyuan and granted an actual fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年十一月，德宗親祀昊天上帝於南郊，震入朝陪祭。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Zhenyuan Emperor Dezong personally sacrificed to High Heaven at the southern altar; Yan Zhen came to court to assist in the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Zhenyuan Emperor Dezong personally sacrificed to High Heaven at the southern altar; Yan Zhen came to court to assist in the rites.

sentences.zh: 十一年二月，加同平章事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eleventh year of Zhenyuan he was granted the title of Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eleventh year of Zhenyuan he was granted the title of Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年六月卒，時年七十六，廢朝三日，冊贈太保，賻布帛米粟有差。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth month of the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan at seventy-six. Court business was suspended for three days; he was posthumously appointed Grand Preceptor, with graded gifts of cloth, silk, grain, and rice.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan at seventy-six. Court business was suspended for three days; he was posthumously appointed Grand Preceptor, with graded gifts of cloth, silk, grain, and rice.

sentences.zh: 及喪將至，令百官以次赴宅吊哭。

translations.literal: When the funeral procession was nearing, the emperor ordered officials to go in turn to his residence to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral procession was nearing, the emperor ordered officials to go in turn to his residence to mourn.

sentences.zh: 嚴礪，震之宗人也。

translations.literal: Yan Li was a kinsman of Yan Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Li was a kinsman of Yan Zhen.

sentences.zh: 性輕躁，多奸謀，以便佞在軍，歷職至山南東道節度都虞候、興州刺史、兼監察御史。

translations.literal: He was impulsive and scheming, and rose in the army through flattery, eventually serving as chief intendant of the East Shannan military commission, prefect of Xing prefecture, and concurrent Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was impulsive and scheming, and rose in the army through flattery, eventually serving as chief intendant of the East Shannan military commission, prefect of Xing prefecture, and concurrent Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年，嚴震卒，以礪權留府事，兼遺表薦礪才堪委任。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan, when Yan Zhen died, Yan Li was left to manage headquarters affairs; Yan Zhen's deathbed memorial also recommended Yan Li as capable of greater responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan, when Yan Zhen died, Yan Li was left to manage headquarters affairs; Yan Zhen's deathbed memorial also recommended Yan Li as capable of greater responsibility.

sentences.zh: 七月，超授興元尹，兼御史大夫，山南西道節度、支度營田、觀察使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was abruptly appointed Governor of Xingyuan, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and military commissioner of Shannan West with charge over supplies, military colonies, and observation.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was abruptly appointed Governor of Xingyuan, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and military commissioner of Shannan West with charge over supplies, military colonies, and observation.

sentences.zh: 詔下，諫官御史以為除拜不當。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, remonstrating officials and censors judged the appointment improper.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, remonstrating officials and censors judged the appointment improper.

sentences.zh: 是日，諫議、給事、補闕、拾遺並歸門下省共議：礪資歷甚淺，人望素輕，遽領節旄，恐非允當。

translations.literal: That day remonstrance officials, reviewing secretaries, and remonstrators all withdrew to the Chancellery to confer: Yan Li's experience was very thin, he had little standing in public opinion, and to rush the military seal on him was hardly fitting.
translations.idiomatic: That day remonstrance officials, reviewing secretaries, and remonstrators all withdrew to the Chancellery to confer: Yan Li's experience was very thin, he had little standing in public opinion, and to rush the military seal on him was hardly fitting.

sentences.zh: 既兼雜話，發論喧然。

translations.literal: Other matters were discussed as well, and the debate grew heated.
translations.idiomatic: Other matters were discussed as well, and the debate grew heated.

sentences.zh: 拾遺李繁獨奏云：「昨除拜嚴礪，眾以為不當，諫議大夫苗拯云：『已三度表論，未見聽允。』

translations.literal: Remonstrator Li Fan alone submitted: "Yesterday's appointment of Yan Li was widely considered improper. Remonstrance Grand Master Miao Zheng said, 'I have already memorialized three times and received no heed.'
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrator Li Fan alone submitted: "Yesterday's appointment of Yan Li was widely considered improper. Remonstrance Grand Master Miao Zheng said, 'I have already memorialized three times and received no heed.'

sentences.zh: 給事中許孟容曰：『誠如此，不曠職矣。』」

translations.literal: Reviewing Secretary Xu Mengrong said, 'If that is so, he has not been derelict in duty.'"
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing Secretary Xu Mengrong said, 'If that is so, he has not been derelict in duty.'"

sentences.zh: 又云：「李元素、陳京、王舒並見拯及孟容言議。」

translations.literal: Li Fan also reported, "Li Yuansu, Chen Jing, and Wang Shu all heard Miao Zheng and Xu Mengrong's exchange."
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan also reported, "Li Yuansu, Chen Jing, and Wang Shu all heard Miao Zheng and Xu Mengrong's exchange."

sentences.zh: 上遣三司使詰之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy from the Three Offices to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy from the Three Offices to investigate.

sentences.zh: 拯狀云：「實於眾中言曾論奏，不言三度。」

translations.literal: Miao Zheng deposed, "I did say in the assembly that I had memorialized, but I did not say three times."
translations.idiomatic: Miao Zheng deposed, "I did say in the assembly that I had memorialized, but I did not say three times."

sentences.zh: 繁證之不已。

translations.literal: Li Fan continued to testify against him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan continued to testify against him.

sentences.zh: 孟容等又云：「拯實言兩度。」

translations.literal: Xu Mengrong and others said, "Miao Zheng actually said two times."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mengrong and others said, "Miao Zheng actually said two times."

sentences.zh: 拯請依眾狀。

translations.literal: Miao Zheng asked to be judged by the majority deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Zheng asked to be judged by the majority deposition.

sentences.zh: 翌日，貶拯萬州刺史，李繁播州參軍，並同正。

translations.literal: The next day Miao Zheng was demoted to prefect of Wan prefecture and Li Fan to staff officer at Bo prefecture, both retaining regular rank.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Miao Zheng was demoted to prefect of Wan prefecture and Li Fan to staff officer at Bo prefecture, both retaining regular rank.

sentences.zh: 礪在位貪殘，士民不堪其苦。

translations.literal: In office Yan Li was greedy and brutal, and officials and commoners alike could not endure the misery.
translations.idiomatic: In office Yan Li was greedy and brutal, and officials and commoners alike could not endure the misery.

sentences.zh: 素惡鳳州刺史馬勛，誣奏貶賀州司戶。

translations.literal: He had long hated Feng prefecture governor Ma Xun and brought a false charge that got Ma Xun demoted to registrar of He prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He had long hated Feng prefecture governor Ma Xun and brought a false charge that got Ma Xun demoted to registrar of He prefecture.

sentences.zh: 縱情肆志，皆此類也。

translations.literal: He indulged his every whim; this was typical of his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He indulged his every whim; this was typical of his conduct.

sentences.zh: 元和四年三月卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third month of the fourth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of the fourth year of Yuanhe (809).

sentences.zh: 卒後，御史元稹奉使兩川按察，糾劾礪在任日贓罪數十萬。

translations.literal: After his death the censor Yuan Zhen was sent on an inspection mission to the two Sichuan circuits and impeached Yan Li for embezzling several hundred thousand in office.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the censor Yuan Zhen was sent on an inspection mission to the two Sichuan circuits and impeached Yan Li for embezzling several hundred thousand in office.

sentences.zh: 詔征其贓，以死，恕其罪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered recovery of the embezzled funds, but because he was dead his crimes were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered recovery of the embezzled funds, but because he was dead his crimes were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：爵人於朝，與眾共之；

translations.literal: The historian writes: To ennoble a man at court is to share the decision with the public;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: To ennoble a man at court is to share the decision with the public;

sentences.zh: 刑人於市，與眾棄之。

translations.literal: To punish a man at the marketplace is to cast him out together with the public.
translations.idiomatic: To punish a man at the marketplace is to cast him out together with the public.

sentences.zh: 縊崔寧，除嚴礪，時君之政可知矣，輔相之才可見矣！

translations.literal: To strangle Cui Ning and appoint Yan Li—the ruler's governance of the time can be known, and the chancellor's talent can be seen!
translations.idiomatic: To garrote Cui Ning while elevating Yan Li—what that says about the emperor's rule and his ministers' judgment needs no further comment!

sentences.zh: 武不稟父風，有違母誨，凡為人子者，得不戒哉！

translations.literal: Wu did not inherit his father's manner and violated his mother's teaching—every man who is a son, can he not take warning!
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wu failed to live up to his father's example and defied his mother's counsel—what son would not take that as a warning!

sentences.zh: 雖有周、孔之才，不足稱也，況狂夫乎！

translations.literal: Even with the talents of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius he would not be worth praising—how much less a reckless man!
translations.idiomatic: Even men with the gifts of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius would not deserve praise for such conduct—how much less a reckless bully!

sentences.zh: 英乂失政，其死也宜哉。

translations.literal: Guo Yingyi lost good government; his death was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yingyi's misrule made his violent end only fitting.

sentences.zh: 嚴震立功，其道也顯矣。

translations.literal: Yan Zhen established merit; his Way is manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhen's loyal service stands in bright contrast—his merit speaks for itself.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：英乂失政，崔寧廢身。

translations.literal: Praise-text says: Guo Yingyi lost good government; Cui Ning ruined himself.
translations.idiomatic: In summary: Guo Yingyi fell through misrule; Cui Ning destroyed himself.

sentences.zh: 武為士子，震作純臣。

translations.literal: Wu was a scholar's son; Zhen acted as a pure minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wu disgraced his scholar's upbringing; Yan Zhen proved a loyal servant of the throne.
